docs.title: Development guide
docs.text: This tutorial will guide you through on how to set up a working environment for developing pynxtools-foo.

docs.title: What should you should know before this tutorial?
docs.text:
• You should read the guide on getting started with pynxtools.
  • You should read the installation tutorial.

docs.title: What you will know at the end of this tutorial?
docs.text:
You will know

  • how to setup your environment for developing pynxtools-foo
  • how to make changes to the software
  • how to test the software
  • how to contribute on GitHub
  • how to use pynxtools-foo as a NOMAD plugin

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Structure of the pynxtools-foo repository

The software tools are located inside src/pynxtools_foo. They are shipped with unit tests located in tests.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
It is recommended to use python 3.12 with a dedicated virtual environment for this package. Learn how to manage python versions and virtual environments. We recommend using uv, an extremely fast manager Python package and project manager. In this tutorial, you will find paralleled descriptions, using either uv or a more classical approach using venv and pip.

Start by creating a virtual environment:

uvvenv

uv is capable of creating a virtual environment and install the required Python version at the same time.

uv venv --python 3.12

Note that you will need to install the Python version manually beforehand.

python -m venv .venv

That command creates a new virtual environment in a directory called .venv.

docs.title: Development installation
docs.text:
We start by cloning the repository:

git clone https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/pynxtools-foo.git \\
    --branch main \\
    --recursive pynxtools-foo
cd pynxtools-foo

Next, we install the package in editable mode (together with its dependencies):

uvpip 
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

Note that you will need to install the Python version manually beforehand.

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: Linting and formatting
docs.text:
We are using ruff and mypy for linting, formatting, and type checking. It is recommended to use the pre-commit hook available for ruff which formats the code and checks the linting before actually making an actual Git commit.

Install the precommit by running

pre-commit install

from the root of this repository.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
There exist unit tests for the software written in pytest which can be used as follows:

pytest -sv tests

docs.title: Editing the documentation
docs.text:
We are using `mkdocs for the documentation. If you edit the documentation, you can build it locally. For this, you need to install an additional set of dependencies:

uvpip 
uv pip install -e ".[docs]"

pip install -e ".[docs]"

You can then serve the documentation locally by running

mkdocs serve

docs.title: Contributing to the package on GitHub
docs.text: Once you are happy with the changes, please commit them on a separate branch and create a pull request on GitHub. We run a number of GitHub actions that check the correct linting, run the tests in an isolated environment, and build the documentation. Once these pass and a peer review of the code has occurred, your code will be accepted.

docs.title: Developing pynxtools-foo as a NOMAD plugin
docs.text: If you plan to contribute to the NOMAD plugin functionality of pynxtools-foo, it often makes sense to use the NOMAD development environment called nomad-distro-dev. You can learn more in the NOMAD documentation.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If you face any issues with the tool or when setting up the development environment, please create a new Github Issue.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
It is recommended to use python 3.12 with a dedicated virtual environment for this package. Learn how to manage python versions and virtual environments.

There are many alternatives to managing virtual environments and package dependencies (requirements). We recommend using uv, an extremely fast manager Python package and project manager. In this tutorial, you will find paralleled descriptions, using either uv or a more classical approach using venv and pip.

Start by creating a virtual environment:

uvvenv

uv is capable of creating a virtual environment and install the required Python version at the same time.

uv venv --python 3.12

Note that you will need to install the Python version manually beforehand.

python -m venv .venv

That command creates a new virtual environment in a directory called .venv.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the latest stable version of this package from PyPI with

uvpip 
uv pip install pynxtools-foo

pip install pynxtools-foo

You can also install the latest development version with

uvpip 
uv pip install git+https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/pynxtools-foo.git

pip install git+https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/pynxtools-foo.git

docs.title: How to install pynxtools-foo with NOMAD
docs.text: To use pynxtools-foo with NOMAD, simply install it in the same environment as the nomad-lab package. NOMAD will recognize pynxtools-foo as a plugin automatically. In addition, NOMAD will install a schema for NeXus application definitions.
